figures.finding: Antigua and Barbuda levies no income tax on an individual's pay: the Personal Income Tax ran from April 2005 to June 2016 and was repealed; a self-employed person instead pays the Unincorporated Business Tax on net business income, 0% to EC$42,000, 8% to EC$186,000 and 25% above (sole trader).
figures.applies: Employment income: none since 1 July 2016. UBT: self-employment, sole-proprietor and partnership income; partnership bands widen by EC$42,000 per partner.

sources.said: The Unincorporated Business Tax came into effect from July 1, 2016 after the repeal of the Personal Income Tax (April 2005-June 2016)

figures.finding: From 1 January 2025 a private-sector employee pays 7% and the employer 9% of insurable earnings to Social Security (16% in all), on earnings up to EC$6,500 a month; a self-employed person pays 10% of declared earnings between the minimum wage and EC$6,500 a month; Medical Benefits takes 3.5% from employee and employer each, and 5% of a self-employed person's earnings.

figures.finding: Nothing is withheld for income tax from a resident's pay, since none is levied; a self-employed person pays UBT by quarterly instalments due the 15th after each quarter and files the annual return by 31 March.
figures.applies: Social security and medical benefits are still deducted from pay.

figures.finding: A person in Antigua and Barbuda paying a non-resident individual income chargeable there (a performer's or director's fee for work done there among it) withholds 25% and remits it by the 15th of the next month; the tax withheld is credited against the non-resident's final liability, so it is not final.
figures.applies: Non-resident individuals paid for income chargeable in Antigua and Barbuda (Unincorporated Business Tax Act 2016 s. 17; Income Tax Act Cap. 212 s. 40), unless a treaty reduces the rate. No rule specific to performers exists in either Act.

figures.finding: Antigua and Barbuda Sales Tax is charged at 17% (from 1 January 2024) on supplies of a business with taxable supplies of EC$300,000 or more a year; professional service providers must register whatever their turnover.

figures.finding: Neither the Income Tax Act nor the Unincorporated Business Tax Act treats authors' fees or royalties specially: a resident author's royalties are taxed with other business income under the Unincorporated Business Tax as income arising from property, and royalties paid to a non-resident bear the 25% withholding.
